problem:
Given that the differential equation

$$
{x}^{2}{y}^{″}+15x{y}^{′}+49y=0
$$

has the general solution

$$
y={c}_{1}{x}^{-7}+{c}_{2}{x}^{-7}\operatorname{ln}⁡x,
$$

solve the initial value problem

$$
{x}^{2}{y}^{″}+15x{y}^{′}+49y=0,\,y(1)=1,\,{y}^{′}(1)=1,\,x>0.
$$
worked_solution:
We find the constants ${c}_{1}$ and ${c}_{2}$ using the initial conditions.

- First, we apply the condition $y(1)=1.$ Substituting $y(1)=1$ into the general solution gives

$$
1={c}_{1}.
$$

- Then, we apply the condition ${y}^{′}(1)=1.$ Differentiating $y,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & =-7{c}_{1}{x}^{-8}+{c}_{2}{x}^{-8}-7{c}_{2}{x}^{-8}\operatorname{ln}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting ${y}^{′}(1)=1$ and ${c}_{1}=1$ into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}1 & =-7(1)+{c}_{2} \\ {c}_{2} & =8.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution to the initial value problem is

$$
\begin{aligned}y(x) & ={x}^{-7}+8{x}^{-7}\operatorname{ln}⁡x \\  & =\frac{1+8\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{{x}^{7}}.\end{aligned}
$$
